abstract.t: Evolution of the 6G user plane toward distributed Serving and Anchor User Plane Functions (S-UPFs and A-UPFs) offers an opportunity to coordinate mobility, IP transport, and application/AI-compute placement. This document explores an architecture in which a Mobile User Plane Controller (MUP-C) translates authorized mobile-session information and transport-aware steering decisions into BGP Mobile User Plane (MUP) routing information. It describes interworking with the BGP MUP SAFI, access and data-network segments, SRv6 forwarding, mobility, and user-plane accounting. The architecture is transport- neutral; SRv6 is an illustrative data plane. The proposed application-to-session binding and 6G procedures are for discussion and do not define new BGP encodings or change 3GPP procedures.
